blocks.text: Condo buildings in Chilliwack Proper West
The Robson — 9450 Robson Street

The building directory records The Robson as built in 2022, with 60 units, amenities elevator, garden and in-suite laundry, and strata bylaws recorded as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. Current listings record the building differently on year: multiple listings state built 2023, with sub-type Apartment/Condo (one records Apartment), 4 storeys, freehold strata ownership, frame-wood construction, underground parking, and listing amenity sets that add clubhouse, exercise centre and caretaker to the directory's list. Listings describe the building as in the revitalized downtown core, a short walk to District 1881.

items.t: Chilliwack Proper West is the west half of "Chilliwack Proper," the board grouping for the city-proper (downtown-side) part of Chilliwack, as distinct from the Sardis / Vedder / Garrison side south of Highway 1. No board-published boundary for "Chilliwack Proper West" exists: Not verified as an official boundary. Nearby areas: Chilliwack Proper East and downtown Chilliwack (District 1881) to the east, Fairfield Island to the north, and Sardis / Vedder Crossing south of Highway 1.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the downtown/hospital side. The one apartment-condo building verified by name stands on Robson Street in the revitalized downtown core near District 1881, and the verified townhouse stock clusters on Wolfe Road across from Townsend Park.
District structure: SD33 has nineteen elementary schools (Kindergarten to Grade 5), four middle schools (Grades 6 to 8), two K-8 schools and five secondary schools (Grades 9–12).
Published drive times: Not verified.
Addresses and facility details for these on a City of Chilliwack facility page: Not verified pass.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Chilliwack Proper West

items.t: Secondary suites and ADUs: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 defines a secondary suite as an accessory dwelling unit of not more than 90 m² and less than 40% of the habitable floor space of the building, located within a building containing only 1 principal dwelling unit — the cap is the lesser of 90 m² and 40%. Section 4.06(1) permits only 1 ADU per lot where the zone permits an ADU (secondary suite, coach house or garden suite), and garden suites are capped at 100 m² by Section 4.06(1)(g). The City's Secondary Suites Policy permits the rental of secondary suites within any single detached dwelling in the City regardless of zone; a suite must be built with a building permit, meet the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new secondary suites are not permitted below the flood construction level under the Floodplain Regulation Bylaw.

Flood and ALR: flood hazard zoning exists in the bylaw structure (RS-FHA reserve zone, Section 12.02 of Bylaw No. 5000) and the City applies flood protection requirements and a Floodplain Regulation Bylaw; parcel-level Flood Construction Levels for Chilliwack Proper West lots are not verified. Properties in the Agricultural Land Reserve are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR regulations, and the City directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap; ALR land inside the Chilliwack Proper West working scope is not verified (the scope is the urban city-proper side), and ALR residences cannot be stratified in any case (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).

items.t: This market runs on a different board's numbers — or none. Chilliwack trades on CADREB, SnapStats does not cover the city, and CADREB publishes board-wide figures only.

The Robson's build year disagrees between the directory and its own listings. Directory: 2022. Listings: 2023, consistently. The difference matters for warranty stage and depreciation-report timing, and it settles only on the registered strata plan — a buyer's agent should not repeat either year as settled until then.
One Wolfe Road complex has no citable name.

The downtown condo sits inside a form-and-character permit area. OCP Bylaw 5500's Schedule D-6 makes the whole downtown a Form & Character Development Permit Area under Local Government Act s. 488(1)(d), with the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan and Downtown Design Guidelines behind it — exterior alterations and redevelopment around The Robson run through that lens, not just the zoning bylaw.

The hospital is the area's true anchor, and it is a Fraser Health community hospital — primary, core secondary and some specialty services at 45600 Menholm Road, on the Hodgins Avenue side of the Proper West ground, minutes from both the Robson Street and Wolfe Road strata stock.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Chilliwack Proper West

items.t: City plan — standing correction carried: the current Official Community Plan is Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw No. 5500; in that framework the Sardis plan is Schedule B5 and the Agricultural Plan is Schedule B1.

Zoning, SSMUH, suites and ADUs: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 governs; its Section 6 sets the agricultural zones, Section 7 the rural zones, and Section 12 includes the RS-FHA (Flood Hazard Area) reserve zone. SSMUH: Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395, adopted June 18, 2024, allows 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing. A secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the building's habitable floor space (Bylaw No. 5000, s. 2); only 1 ADU per lot where the zone permits (s. 4.06(1) — secondary suite, coach house or garden suite), and garden suites are capped at 100 m². The City's Secondary Suites Policy permits rental of a suite in any single detached dwelling regardless of zone, with a building permit, BC Building and Fire Code compliance and flood-protection compliance; new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level.

Chilliwack property taxes: notices are mailed annually at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1 of every calendar year; a 5% penalty applies for taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% for taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026. This staged 5% + 5% is Chilliwack's own city scheme — do not confuse it with Mission's flat 10%, or with the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime (whose second stage runs at October 31 and is paid to the Province).

items.t: Zoning — City of Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: Its Section 6 sets the agricultural (farm) zones and Section 7 the rural zones, and Section 12 includes the RS-FHA (Flood Hazard Area) reserve zone.

SSMUH — Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395, adopted June 18, 2024: allows 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing, per the City's staff report and the amendment record in the consolidated Zoning Bylaw No. 5000.

Suites and ADUs (Bylaw No. 5000, ss. 2 and 4.06): only 1 ADU per lot where the zone permits an ADU; a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the habitable floor space of the building and must sit within a building containing only 1 principal dwelling unit; garden suites are capped at 100 m². The City's Secondary Suites Policy permits rental of secondary suites within any single detached dwelling regardless of zone, built with a permit and to BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements; new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level.

Property taxes (City of Chilliwack): notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1 each year; for 2026, a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026.

Proper West's plan is a schedule, not the city-wide text alone: the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan sits as Schedule B-2 of OCP Bylaw No. 5500, and the 2050 OCP review folded its land uses into city-wide designations while its neighbourhood policies remain in the plan — a lot buyer reading only the OCP's general residential policies misses the Proper-specific layer.

Strata vs freehold split and age/style profile of the stock: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Chilliwack Proper West

items.t: Plan and zoning (Chilliwack): Land use sits under the City's 2050 Official Community Plan (Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500), whose Schedule B2 is the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan; the guide states the plan's designations as Residential 1 (one and two family housing) and Residential 2 (attached housing and narrow lot infill), quoted in a City public hearing notice dated May 4, 2021 for a rezoning inside the plan area. Zoning is Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000. Any parcel's actual zone is per-parcel: Not verified. Chilliwack's Supreme Court registry position: Not confirmed.

SSMUH (Chilliwack's own position): Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395, amending Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000, adopted June 18, 2024, allows 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing — duplexes are the baseline form where it applies.

Under Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000, a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the habitable floor space of the building (s.2); only 1 accessory dwelling unit may be located on a lot, with permitted types including secondary suite, coach house and garden suite, garden suites capped at 100 m² (s.4.06(1)); ADU parking is 1 space for a 1-bedroom ADU or any secondary suite and 2 spaces for a 2-or-more-bedroom coach or garden suite (s.5.04); a suite must be built with a building permit, meet the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new secondary suites are not permitted below the flood construction level. So a Chilliwack duplex carries at most ONE accessory unit on its lot on this rule — a suite inside one half does not create a second ADU for the other half.
